title: Handgrip Strength Measurement as a Functional Biomarker in Resectable Esophageal or Stomach Cancer: A Prospective Investigation Throughout the Surgical-Oncological Treatment Course
summary: This study investigates whether handgrip strength is associated with the course of cancer treatment. Handgrip strength is measured at predefined time points, and changes in handgrip strength during treatment are assessed. In addition, nutritional status, questionnaire data, body composition, and information on the course of treatment are collected. Particular attention is given to possible associations between handgrip strength and complications, treatment delays or discontinuation, and recovery after surgery. The aim of the study is to determine whether the simple measurement of handgrip strength may provide useful information about the course of treatment.

interventions.name:
Isometric handgrip strength is measured using a Jamar® hand dynamometer (Sammons Preston Rolyan, Bolingbrook, IL, USA). The measurement is performed on the dominant hand in a seated position, with the elbow extended, the shoulder and forearm in a neutral position, and without arm support.
Participa

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed, resectable esophageal carcinoma with an indication for surgical oncological treatment; written informed consent to participate in the study following appropriate information and consent procedures.
Exclusion criteria:
Unresectable esophageal carcinoma; inability to provide informed consent or absence of written informed consent to participate in the study; physical limitations or disorders of the upper extremity that prevent standardized measurement of handgrip strength.
